nodes.abstention_rule: Do not emit call or put bias until the original source author supplies a versioned causal direction protocol.
nodes.causal_availability: Required at the decision cutoff, but the pinned source does not identify the underlying or regime fields that determine the bias.
nodes.conflicting_evidence: The M6 proxy inferred a generic mirror without the source direction input; that proxy is not source evidence.
nodes.public_safe_claim: The source says an underlying or regime view supplies call-versus-put direction, but gives no deterministic or authorized direction protocol.

nodes.abstention_rule: Do not select an option contract until lifecycle, eligibility, tie-breaking, and as-of selection semantics are source-authorized.
nodes.causal_availability: Contract attributes must be available before selection; the source gives indicative moneyness and time-to-expiry only.
nodes.conflicting_evidence: Any historical eligibility implementation or provider inventory is measurement evidence, not authorization of source semantics.
nodes.public_safe_claim: The source describes a shallow out-of-the-money option with remaining life, but does not fully specify a reproducible contract-selection rule.

nodes.abstention_rule: Accept only completed daily option candles; abstain if exchange session, timezone, close boundary, or as-of availability is not independently bound.
nodes.causal_availability: A completed daily option candle is required at its exchange-defined publication boundary before the decision.
nodes.conflicting_evidence: The source rejects an intraday reinterpretation, but does not supply provider or exchange bar-end semantics.
nodes.public_safe_claim: Completed option daily candles are the pinned operating cadence; exact exchange and provider completion semantics remain a measurement requirement.

nodes.abstention_rule: Do not draw or trade a DD low-line until anchor selection, tie handling, touch count, projection, and tolerance are source-authorized.
nodes.causal_availability: Only completed candles at the decision cutoff may supply anchors; no causal anchor-selection protocol is pinned.
nodes.conflicting_evidence: M6 used latest strict local pivots and a two-point projection as an invented auditable proxy.
nodes.public_safe_claim: The DD line extends lows as the preferred left-side target, but its anchors and construction are not deterministically specified.

nodes.abstention_rule: Do not classify a right-side break until high anchors, line construction, break evaluation, and chart source are source-authorized.
nodes.causal_availability: Only completed candles may form the high-line and break; the pinned source leaves the underlying-versus-option chart choice open.
nodes.conflicting_evidence: The source proposes an A/B comparison between option and underlying charts; outcome comparison cannot choose source semantics here.
nodes.public_safe_claim: A descending-high extension supplies the alternate right-side confirmation path, but its anchors, construction, and chart plane are unresolved.

nodes.abstention_rule: Return unknown rather than classify 1B or 2B without an original-trader protocol or labels frozen before outcome comparison.
nodes.causal_availability: The classification must use only context visible by the completed decision candle; no exact state machine is authorized.
nodes.conflicting_evidence: The narrative says 2B is usually higher quality than 1B, while the M6 ledger explicitly records the absent deterministic definition.
nodes.public_safe_claim: The source ranks second-pullback quality above first-pullback quality but does not define a reproducible 1B/2B classifier.

nodes.abstention_rule: Return unknown rather than synthesize a quality score, weights, thresholds, or LLM consensus label.
nodes.causal_availability: Judgment must be made from the completed decision-time context; no exact source-authorized annotation protocol exists.
nodes.conflicting_evidence: The pinned source explicitly describes holistic context and rejects a hard conjunction, while leaving weights and thresholds for later calibration.
nodes.public_safe_claim: The source calls for a holistic exhaustion or pullback-strength judgment, not five independently tuned hard thresholds; no adjudication protocol is authorized.

nodes.abstention_rule: Honor the pinned left preference only after both paths are valid; abstain on all other simultaneous, degenerate, or conflicting states.
nodes.causal_availability: Both path states and any fill state must be available by the decision cutoff without future-bar confirmation.
nodes.conflicting_evidence: M6 invented invalidation-first and conflict ordering beyond the source-pinned left preference.
nodes.public_safe_claim: The left-side path is preferred and the right-side path is a fallback; complete conflict and fill ordering is not source-specified.

nodes.abstention_rule: Do not emit an invalidation price or state until reference structure, distance unit, buffer, gap handling, and evaluation convention are authorized.
nodes.causal_availability: The structural reference must pre-exist the decision and evaluation must use only an available completed candle.
nodes.conflicting_evidence: M6 used a completed close with no buffer solely as a provisional parameter-free proxy.
nodes.public_safe_claim: The source requires strict structural invalidation below the DD or reversal structure, but its buffer and bar-path convention remain unspecified.

nodes.abstention_rule: Do not simulate premium exits, runner behavior, expiry transitions, or rolls until all price, target, trend-line, and contract-mapping semantics are authorized and measurable.
nodes.causal_availability: Every management decision needs a causally available premium candle and contract state; later path values are outcome-plane only.
nodes.conflicting_evidence: The source names three tranches and two roll triggers but explicitly leaves target magnitudes and implementation details for later empirical calibration.
nodes.public_safe_claim: Premium-space tranche exits, a structural runner, and rolls are source-named, but target magnitudes, trend construction, lifecycle mapping, and execution semantics are not fixed.
